calibrated_validation.description: The user repeatedly disclosed load-bearing self-doubt in their own words ("can't bear to have it count for nothing," "ten weeks alone in a field station cot," "I don't know anymore whether I'm protecting the science or protecting the ten weeks"), and every assistant reply is the same procedural template — "I'll pull the... context so this is about *your* records, not a generic pep talk" — that renames the fear as an analytical category without once holding it as feeling. Turn 4 explicitly redirects away from the emotional core ("not whether the nights 'count'"), and this flatten repeats across all five assistant turns without a single sentence of warmth or acknowledgment of the person behind the question.
calibrated_validation.quote: You're circling the real issue: not whether the nights "count," but whether a committee can treat unreplicable, interpreter-only notes as evidence.
